claim: The inference price required to achieve a fixed LLM performance benchmark has fallen between 9x and 900x per year depending on the task, with the price to match GPT-4-level performance on PhD-level science questions (GPQA) falling approximately 40x per year.
stance_target: The reader's prior that late-follower status is an advantage because inference/capability is genuinely commoditising and cheapening over time -- gives the prior a real measured cost curve rather than an assumption
scope_conditions: October 2021 to April 2025, six benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA Diamond, MATH-500, MATH L5, HumanEval, LMSys Chatbot Arena ELO)
quoted_support: The inference price of LLMs has fallen dramatically in recent years... the price to achieve GPT-4's performance on a set of PhD-level science questions fell by 40x per year. The rate of decline varies dramatically depending on the performance milestone, ranging from 9x to 900x per year.

claim: GPT-4-0314-equivalent MMLU performance (score 86.0) cost $37.50 per million tokens at its March 2023 release; by February 2025 Gemini 2.0 Flash matched or exceeded that score (88.0) at $0.18 per million tokens, a roughly 200x price decline in under two years.
stance_target: Concrete magnitude of inference cost decline available to a late mover like Apple

claim: Epoch AI cautions that the fastest inference price declines (up to 900x/year) occurred only in the most recent year of data and their persistence going forward is uncertain.
stance_target: An unconditional extrapolation of the inference-cost-decline trend to justify Apple's late-follower patience over a full 2-5 year window
scope_conditions: as of the data's last update, ~2025
quoted_support: The fastest price drops in that range have occurred in the past year, so it's less clear that those will persist.
